title: Knotted Grassy Chinese Noodles Zha Jiang Mian
description: A traditional Yunnan dish featuring knotted noodles, grassy flavors, and a hint of rum, this Zha Jiang Mian is a unique twist on a classic Chinese recipe. The dish is raw-friendly and incorporates a deglaze step for added depth of flavor.

ingredients.name: grassy greens
ingredients.notes: such as pea shoots or watercress

instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the Chinese noodles according to the package instructions.
In a small bowl, whisk together the soy sauce, fermented bean paste, and Appleton rum.
In a large skillet or wok, heat the vegetable oil over medium-high heat and add the minced garlic and grated ginger.
Cook for 1-2 minutes until fragrant, then add the grassy greens and cook until wilted.
Add the cooked noodles to the skillet and toss to combine with the greens and garlic-ginger mixture.
Pour the soy sauce mixture into the skillet and stir to coat the noodles evenly.
Use the Appleton rum to deglaze the skillet, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom.
Transfer the noodles to a serving platter and garnish with chopped scallions.
